text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The Australian sharemarket peaked yesterday and bond interest rates tumbled as financial markets anticipated an early interest rate cut from the Reserve Bank after figures released by the Australian Bureau of Statistics revealed wages growth is under contol. A rise of 0.7 per cent in ordinary-time pay during the three months to August, and growth of 3.5 per cent over the past year, have fulfilled the RBA's pre-condition for rate cuts. Page 1.

Accounting firm Deloitte Touche Tomastu's resource tax partner John Leahy said yesterday the firm has called on the Government to review the capital gains tax on mergers, saying the tax was intended to apply only to realised gains, and mergers rarely involved such a gain. The move came as competition policy experts called for a review of Australia's tough merger laws. Page 3.

Despite a lessening of wages growth revealed in yesterday's average weekly ordinary time earnings (AWOTE), there are two dangers on the horizon for wage-push inflation: one is the big wage rises in formal enterprise agreements during the past two quarters and the second is the ACTU's "living wage" claim. Page 4.

BHP has gained a waiver from the Australian Stock Exchange to allow it to withhold sensitive petroleum excavation information from the share market when drilling in foreign-controlled waters and in the Timor Gap Zone of Co-operation. It is likely BHP will make an application for similar waivers for drilling in Australian waters. Page 33.

Seven Network chairman Kerry Stokes said he believes the network could own Optus Vision outright if it is successful in its legal action against other Optus Vision shareholders Publishing and Broadcasting, Optus Communications, and US-based Continental Calevision. Page 33.

Colly Cotton Ltd debuted on the Australian Stock Exchange yesterday at an 11 percent premium to its A$1 issue price. Colly shares closed at A$1.12, indicating investors are unfazed by the uncertainty of the agricultural sector. Page 39.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian financial markets reached fever pitch yesterday with the expectation of lower interest rates becoming a reality after the release of figures showing wages growth had slowed. The All Ordinaries reached a record close of 2377.6 points, with investors anticipating a 0.5 per cent cut in short-term rates when the Reserve Bank board meets on November 5. Page 23.

News Corporation has announced plans to raise A$1.28 billion by issuing preference shares convertible into shares in its UK satellite service British Sky Broadcasting. The move will lift the media giant's cash on hand funds to almost A$4 billion. The shareissue will reduce News' holdings in BSkyB to 35 per cent from current holdings of 40 per cent. Page 23.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has initiated court action which could see programming agreements between the Nine Network, the Seven Network SVN.AX and the Golden West Network dissolved. The ACCC believes the programme agreements to be anti-cometitive after finding the deals breached the Trade Practices Act. Page 23.

Seven Network Ltd chairman Kerry Stokes has announced the broadcaster would bid for full control of pay-TV operator Optus Vision, pending the outcome of a hostile legal action against fellow shareholders in the pay-TV group Optus Communications, Publishing & Broadcasting Ltd and Continental Cable Vision. The action is aimed at retaining entitled rights which Seven believes has been eroded by an arrangement between the three defendants. Page 23.

Newcrest Mining Ltd chairman Sir Rod Carnegie has told a shareholders' meeting there would be no repeat of the debacle of the Normandy Mining Ltd investment deal. Following Newcrest's' current A$107 million loss on its A$470 million investment in the Normndy Group, Carnegie assured an angry shareholder "we ain't going to do it again". Page 25.

Westpac Banking Corp returned to the spotlight yesterday following comments from John Strickland, chairman of Hongkong & Shanghai Bank Corp, a possible predator of the Westpac Bank. Strickland's comments fuelled speculation that the London-based bank could acquire Westpac in the near future. Westpac shares finished the day 10 cents higher at A$6.94. Page 25.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

While economists are divided on when it will take place, the majority agree that a cut in interest rates is a near certainty. Financial markets seized on the release of the lower-than-expected wages figures with the All Ordinaries surging 30.9 points to 277.6. The wages increase of 0.7 per cent for the three months to August fell well below market expectations of one per cent for the quarter. Page 25.

Seven Network chairman Kerry Stokes has furthered his attack on pay-TV group Optus Communications, saying there was no quick resolution to the court action against Seven's fellow Optus Vision investors - Continental Cablevision, Optus Communications and Pblishing and Broadcasting (PBL). Seven has accused the investors of breaching the shareholders' agreement in August by altering the terms of PBL's option agreement. Page 25.

Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation will increase its cash holdings to A$4.5 billion by raising US$1 billion through the issue of a hybrid debt-security instrument called Exchangeable Trust Originated Preferred Securities (TOPrS) to institutional shareholders. Page 25.

AMP Investments fixed interest strategist Chris Loong believes Australia's improved inflation performance has seen the country benefit from the influx of money into local bonds by global investors. The spread between the yields on US and Australian ten-yar bonds has narrowed down to just 0.81 percentage points. Overseas investors believe the inflation performance is sustainable. Page 25.

Capital Property Trust (CPT), owned by Sydney's millionaire Snow brothers, may be put up for sale, after the group announced yesterday it was re-examining the future of the fund and its management. The Snow's Capital Property Management, the listed trusts manager, is seeking expressions of interests for a strategic alliance. Page 27.

Reef Casino Trust RCT.AX chairman John Coates announced at yesterday's annual general meeting that the debt-laden trust would look at a major shake-up of its operations, which will probably focus on the removal of the casino's operator Casinos Australia. Page 27
THE AGE

The All Ordinaries reached a record high of 2377.6 points yesterday, in the wake of the release of Australian Bureau of Statistics average weekly earnings data that pointed towards an interest rate cut by Christmas. Economists believe the weekly earnings data, combined with figures released earlier in the week showing the lowest increase in headline inflation in two years, should soothe the Reserve Bank's fears of a wages blow-out. Page C1.

Joseph Gutnick's Centaur Mining & Exploration last night reported another gold discovery in Western Australia, this time at its Quarters deposit on Centaur's Mount Pleasant tenements, 30 kilometres north-west of Kalgoorlie. The deposit now has a resource base of 810,000 ounces. Page C1.

In response to the questioning of one aggravated shareholder who took his company to task for its A$470 million plunge into Normandy Mining, Newcrest Mining chairman Sir Roderick Carnegie yesterday assured shareholders that the failed attempt to force a mrger deal with Normandy was the type of corporate play it would not be involved in again. Page C1.

Australis Media have failed in their hope of raising US$150 million through a secured bond issue in the United States, after apparently going to the bond market on Wednesday night offering an interest rate of 16 per cent together with options equating to five per cent of its ordinary shares, yet having the offer snubbed by investors. Page C3.

Seven Network chairman Kerry Stokes told the network's annual general meeting in Melbourne that sales revenue for the first quarter was ahead of budget, despite a slump in advertiser spending. Stokes told the meeting the outlook for the network depended somewhat on whether interest rates are cut. Page C3.

The Australian Stock Exchange yesterday granted BHP a six-month waiver from certain obligations to report on its oil exploration wells outside Australia and in the Timor Sea zone of cooperation with Indonesia. BHP said it would be interested in being part of a review of the reporting rules. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
